page.title: Data Import
page.description: Upload a supported xlsx for classification and review. The system proposes a data type and adapter for P&L, Balance Sheet, Cash Flow, operational KPI, CAPEX, sales, land, company descriptions, holding structure, budget actuals, or sales forecast. A proposal is not proof that an arbitrary workbook is mapped correctly: review routing, accounts, conflicts, scope, and reconciliation before applying.
page.stackLine: Flow: explicit upload and Analyze → saved template or AI classifier → adapter preview → review and reconciliation → explicit Apply. A saved template can skip the paid classifier; analysis can otherwise invoke Anthropic and store operational preview metadata.
page.safetyTitle: Viewing this page is read-only; workflow actions are not.
page.safetyBody: Selecting a file is local, but Analyze can upload its contents, call a paid AI provider, and create preview or staging records. Apply writes imported financial data. Cleanup is a separate destructive workflow that can archive or delete scoped data. Use each action only with the correct file, authority, and explicit intent.

cleanup.title: Do you need to delete anything first?
cleanup.body: No. Uploading a file again replaces the years and companies that file covers — the old rows for those years are removed automatically. Delete data only when you want it gone from the system entirely.

alertHistory.title: Alert evaluation snapshot
alertHistory.description: Latest successfully persisted evaluator-match snapshot for period {period}. When a later evaluation snapshot is successfully persisted after recompute, it atomically replaces the previous set for the same organization and period; this is not a complete run history or live monitoring.
alertHistory.scopeBody: Rows prove only that a rule matched when this snapshot was persisted. They do not prove the condition is still current, acknowledged, resolved, or decision-grade. A persistence failure can leave an older snapshot in place; no rows do not prove that evaluation ran.
alertHistory.filterDisclosure: Filter, reset, and load more issue read-only GET requests. They do not recompute indicators, acknowledge an alert, or call an AI provider.
alertHistory.readingSeverity: Severity is configured rule priority, not an audited probability or financial-materiality rating.
alertHistory.readingMessage: Built-in rules use localized stored keys and parameters. Custom rules can fall back to their stored source-language text.
alertHistory.readingPagination: Load more reads another page of this stored snapshot, not an older recompute run.
alertHistory.readingDeepLink: A terminal link appears only for exactly one company and one affected indicator. The resolver rechecks scope and cell existence; navigation itself does not run AI.
alertHistory.loadFailed: Stored alert matches could not be loaded: {error}
alertHistory.emptyTitle: No stored match rows for period {period}.
alertHistory.emptyBody: Absence is not a green status: it does not prove that an evaluation ran or that current source data has no risk conditions.
alertHistory.continuationTitle: No visible rows in the scanned segment.
alertHistory.continuationBody: More raw snapshot rows remain after scope filtering. Use Load more to continue the read-only scan; this is not a green or definitive empty result.
alertHistory.latestEvaluation: Latest stored evaluation on this page: {date} UTC.
alertHistory.affectedCompanies: {count, plural, one {# affected company} other {# affected companies}}
alertHistory.openTerminalTitle: Open the affected company, indicator, and period in Risk Terminal. This navigation does not run AI.

adminDataArchive.title: Delete and restore data
adminDataArchive.description: Deleting removes data from the risk matrix, from indicator calculations and from reports. Some of it can be brought back from this page; some comes back only when you upload the file again; some is gone for good. Every action is written to the audit trail. This page shows which is which before you confirm.
adminDataArchive.historyEmpty: Nothing has been deleted or restored yet.

adminDataDelete.intro: Removing data is a separate decision from importing it. You do not need to delete anything before uploading a file again — a new import replaces the years and companies it covers on its own. Use this page only when you want data to disappear from the system.

chooser.question: What do you want to do?

clearYears.title: Clear figures for a year
clearYears.body: The numbers for one or more years are wrong and you want them gone. You pick the companies, the years, and what exactly goes.

removeCompany.title: Remove one company's data
removeCompany.body: A company was closed, sold, or loaded by mistake. This removes everything ever imported for it, for every year.

restore.title: Bring back deleted data
restore.body: See what was deleted recently and bring back what can be brought back.

deleteAll.title: Delete everything and start clean
deleteAll.body: Empties the whole group: every company, every year, plus the group-wide sales forecast and the compliance records held against each company. Used before a fresh start.

companies.allSelectedNote: You have selected every company. Two group-level things will also be removed for the years you pick: the sales forecast by department, and old rows that are not linked to any company. Both are listed in the check below.

years.question: Pick one or more years. The numbers are the financial rows held for that year; the exact count is shown at step 4.
years.allChipNote: "All years" also covers rows the chips above do not break down by year — the operational figures and the sales plan. Audit findings, court cases and other year-less records are not deleted; those belong to "Remove one company's data".
years.lockedTooltip: {year} was closed by {who} on {date} — "{reason}". Nothing can be deleted for it.
years.allYearsLocked: An "all years" delete would cover closed periods too, so it is refused. Pick specific open years, or release the lock first.
years.noIndex: The selected companies hold no year-tagged financial rows — the data they do have is not split by year. Pick «All years»; the exact count is at step 4.

what.statementsHint: Profit & loss, balance sheet, cash flow, customers and suppliers.
what.operational: Only the operational figures and actuals loaded from files
what.operationalHint: Tonnes, hectares, headcount, and actuals loaded from files. Figures typed in by hand are not touched. Leaves the statements alone.
what.exactHint: Tick the kinds of data you want gone. The number on the right is the total across all years — the exact count for the years you picked is shown at step 4.
what.indicatorsLocked: Always included. Calculated indicators are cleared together with the data they are calculated from and recalculated straight away — from whatever data is left. Where the source data goes too, they come back empty.

adminStatementControls.pageDescription: Run the six canonical statement-reconciliation controls against a company's imported statements — in shadow mode. The tolerance policy is recorded but not owner-approved and no statement row carries lineage, so every control is provisional (arithmetic evaluated, not certifiable) or blocked (evidence missing) — never pass/fail.
adminStatementControls.noStatements: No financial statements imported for this company yet — nothing to reconcile. Import a workbook first.
adminStatementControls.errorGeneric: Could not run the controls. Please try again.
adminStatementControls.bannerDetail: The tolerance policy is the recorded T-1 Option A shape for shadow methodology only (policy not approved), and no statement row carries lineage (lineage missing). Every control is therefore "provisional" (arithmetic evaluated, not certifiable) or "blocked" (evidence missing) — never pass/fail, by design.
adminStatementControls.bannerTooltip: Shadow surface: results can inform review but must not drive decisions.
adminStatementControls.whyTitle: Why nothing can pass or fail here
adminStatementControls.whyBody: A decision-grade verdict requires an owner-approved policy AND revision lineage on both sides of every control. The policy is pinned at "provisional" and no statement row carries a revision id, so decision eligibility is always false: the arithmetic is computed and disclosed, but no verdict is minted.

reasons.non_finite_value: A side of the equation has no finite value — evidence is missing.
reasons.sign_inversion: The two sides carry opposite signs — a break, surfaced rather than hidden.
reasons.scope_organization_mismatch: The two sides describe different organizations.
reasons.scope_company_mismatch: The two sides describe different companies.
reasons.scope_period_mismatch: The two sides describe different periods.
reasons.scope_basis_mismatch: The two sides describe different bases (plan vs actual).
reasons.currency_mismatch: The two sides are in different currencies.
reasons.unit_mismatch: The two sides use different units.
reasons.source_rows_missing: A side has no source rows behind its figure.
reasons.policy_currency_floor_missing: The policy has no tolerance floor for this currency — the control fails closed.
reasons.policy_not_approved: The tolerance policy is provisional, not owner-approved.
reasons.lineage_missing: No revision lineage exists on the statement rows.

limitations.legacyRows: Legacy rows without a company assignment are excluded from all sums.
limitations.rateIndependence: FX rates come from the manually entered rate history; if the ledger's own rate was typed there, the FX control is blind to a wholesale-wrong rate.
limitations.rateStaleness: Independent FX rates match as the latest rate dated at or before each row's month end and may carry forward from an earlier month; carried-forward matches are flagged per card, and the staleness threshold is an owner methodology decision.

adminReportingPack.title: Monthly reporting pack import
adminReportingPack.intro: Upload “Reporting YYYY.xlsx”. The importer reads the detail sheets (Actual PLF / BS Actual / CF Actual → actual; Budget PLF → budget), splits each by the BU column into entities (AZSF / EDEN / CPC / ProMalt; EJE/AJE/Consolidated are skipped) and writes through the audited per-entity pipeline in one transaction.
adminReportingPack.applyNote: First “Preview” — no DB writes at all. Then “Apply” — clean-slate per entity (the year’s existing data is replaced), with indicator recompute. CF is actual-only (budget CF is not imported: the table has no plan-kind dimension).

form.applyConfirm: Writing to the DB for {year}. Existing AZSF/EDEN/CPC/ProMalt data (P&L/BS/CF + budget P&L) will be replaced with the file’s data (clean-slate per entity). Continue?

adminMultiSheet.intro: Several P&L sheets of one company in one file: AI maps each sheet, you review/edit, see the combined reconciliation, and apply atomically. For a single sheet — the “Any file (AI)” tab.
adminMultiSheet.lessThan2Plf: Fewer than 2 P&L sheets found. For a single sheet use the “Any file (AI)” tab.
adminMultiSheet.noControlData: ℹ No parent totals for auto-reconciliation — check the mapping manually.
adminMultiSheet.failureBlocked: ⛔ {count} sheet(s) failed to parse — commit blocked (all-or-none mode). Otherwise the company’s data would be replaced by a partial set. Fix the problem sheets and refresh the preview.
adminMultiSheet.redBlocked: 🔴 Control total RED — commit hard-blocked (cannot be overridden). Likely column mis-mapping. The server will reject this commit too.
adminMultiSheet.ackReview: Low AI confidence / critical anomaly on one of the sheets — I reviewed the mapping manually.
adminMultiSheet.indicatorsStale: ⚠ some indicators didn’t recompute — retry/check later.

adminUniversal.codeNameRequired: Company code and name are required
adminUniversal.intro: Upload an arbitrary file: AI proposes a column mapping, you review/edit, see the reconciliation with no writes, and only then apply. Phase 1 — a single P&L sheet (balance sheet / cash flow and multi-sheet — later).
adminUniversal.companyOptionalHint: Optional for files with a BU/company column; required for single-company sheets.
adminUniversal.multiCurrencyLabel: 💱 Sheet in multiple currencies — import into:
adminUniversal.currencyHint: rows will be tagged with this currency (BudgetLine.currencyCode)
adminUniversal.multiEntityTitle: 🏢 The sheet contains several companies (entity column)
adminUniversal.multiEntityDesc: Each BU value routes to a separate company. Check the auto-matching; one value — one company. Elimination/consolidation blocks (EJE/AJE/…) can be “Skipped”.
adminUniversal.elimTitle: Looks like an elimination/consolidation — usually not imported
adminUniversal.noControlData: ℹ The file has no parent totals for auto-reconciliation — check the mapping manually.
adminUniversal.redBlocked: 🔴 Control total RED — commit hard-blocked (cannot be overridden). The parent-row total doesn’t match the sum of its leaves: likely column mis-mapping. Fix the mapping and re-run “Preview”. The server will reject this commit too.
adminUniversal.ackControlYellow: 🟡 Small control-total discrepancy (≤1%) reviewed — the parent total ≈ the sum of leaves within rounding.
adminUniversal.ackCritical: AI flagged a critical anomaly (see the table above) — I reviewed the mapping manually.
adminUniversal.ackLowConf: Low AI confidence — I reviewed the column mapping manually.
adminUniversal.planUpdateNote: “Update” will overwrite these companies’ rows in the selected plan. Creating a new actual plan when an actual plan for the year already exists is not advised — it double-counts in the terminal (choose “Update”).
adminUniversal.meDuplicate: ⚠ Several BUs route to one company — that would overwrite data. Assign different companies.
adminUniversal.meRedBlocked: 🔴 Control total RED on one of the companies — commit blocked. Fix the mapping and re-run the preview.
adminUniversal.ackCriticalShort: AI flagged a critical anomaly — I reviewed the mapping manually.
adminUniversal.ackSecondActual: ⚠ An actual plan already exists for this year — a new actual plan double-counts in the terminal. I confirm I want a second actual plan (better to choose “Update an existing one”).
adminUniversal.indicatorsStale: ⚠ some indicators didn’t recompute — open the terminal later/retry.
